source.title: Preemptive LLM Unlearning against Forbidden Capability Acquisition via Gradient Sealing
source.authors: Ke-Mou Li; Qi-Zhou Wang; Yue Wang; Feng-Peng Li; Zhuan Shi; Negar Rostamzadeh; Golnoosh Farnadi; Masashi Sugiyama; Jian-Tao Zhou

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether downstream fine-tuning can acquire or reacquire target capabilities after retrospective unlearning, and evaluates a counter-method. It argues that output suppression alone is insufficient and that the claim needs qualification. Its primary setting is preemptive protection, not the original retrospective unlearning setup.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior prompting and relearning studies, but those cited findings are not rows. The primary tables report several measures; rows below use TOFU ES5 and WMDP F5 to keep the model, setting, and method comparisons separate. Values used only for hyperparameter selection are excluded. The paper reports no quantization, prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language-switching, or direct single-direction ablation attack.
record.test_reason: Most of the study concerns preemptive protection on TOFU starting from a retain-only base that never learned the target facts. Those results measure acquisition of new knowledge, not recovery of unlearned knowledge, so they bear on no version. Only the WMDP 'robust removal' setting bears on the claim. There, Zephyr-7B-β, which already knows the material, is unlearned with NPO, RMU, GSU and others, then attacked by full-parameter fine-tuning on a disjoint half of the forget corpus. That is a new setting with a result on A, B and F.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that retrospective output suppression leaves gradient pathways open to later fine-tuning. GSU (gate sealing plus suppression and retention) reduces downstream acquisition across TOFU and WMDP while keeping benign fine-tunability, without claiming irreversible forgetting. The 'retrospective falls short' evidence comes mainly from a knowledge-absent TOFU setting. On WMDP, GSU's advantage over RMU/NPO is under one accuracy point.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes GSU, a pre-release gradient-sealing method, rather than reproducing the cited retrospective methods. It evaluates several retrospective baselines as comparators under downstream fine-tuning attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across model, prevention setting, benchmark, and defense method. The paper reports that acquisition resistance is partial, that the GSU-versus-NPO+SAM gap narrows over attack epochs, and that fine-tuning partially reverses selected-gate changes. It also states the TOFU disjoint split shares authors and domain structure.

fits_no_version.finding: On TOFU, starting from a base that never learned the target authors, retrospective methods and GSU only modestly reduce later fine-tuning acquisition of those facts. GSU usually gives the lowest ES5/UA90.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preemptive unlearning: pre-release defenses can partially reduce downstream acquisition of never-learned forbidden knowledge.

fits_no_version.finding: Proxy look-ahead channel ranks correlate with acquisition-induced changes (ρ=0.617). Attenuating those channels' gradients reduces acquisition gain by up to 24%. GSU pushes selected gates into the SiLU negative tail, and this is partially reversed by attack.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Localized MLP gate pathways mediate downstream acquisition and can be partially sealed.

record.problems: The supplementary analyses are single runs with no multi-seed error bars or significance tests. Main comparisons use utility calibration and specific attack budgets; TOFU disjoint examples are record-disjoint but share target authors and domain structure. Local gate statistics do not measure whole-network gradients or prove causal isolation. The paper states that evaluation does not cover unrestricted retraining and that proxy coverage may not generalize across domain shifts.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 ES3 and UA90 results, Table 2 F3 and UA90 results, and additional ablation/utility trajectories were not separately extracted; the selected ES5/F5 rows and the directly relevant gate and attack-mechanism results were prioritized. The paper's cited prompting/relearning results were excluded because they are not the study's own results.

untested.parts: Release (pre-attack) WMDP accuracy of unlearned models is not reported, so near-chance release cannot be checked. Prompting and quantization attacks are not tested.

Relearning with few, unrelated or loosely related examples is not tested; the WMDP attack uses about 12k (Bio) or 500 (Cyber) forget-domain documents. The size of recovery relative to release is not separable.
Entirely untested. The pathway and gate analyses are in a knowledge-absent setting or concern GSU's own mechanism; no direction ablation restores knowledge.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context recovery.
GSU is not tested against prompting, quantization, activation-direction attacks, few-shot relearning, or LoRA/other attack procedures on WMDP.

missing.what: Post-attack F5 for the other WMDP defenses (GradDiff, WGA, SatImp, RepNoise, ILU, NPO+SAM), e.g. NPO+SAM Bio 38.47, ILU Bio 39.98. These bear on A/B across methods; rows_left_out declares only F3/UA90.
WMDP F3 and UA90 (utility-filtered max accuracy), e.g. RMU Bio UA90 34.24, GSU 34.98. Declared left out, but needed to compare recovery under utility-preserving attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mislabeled versions as V1–V6. Most rows are TOFU 'prevention', where the base model never learned the facts, so they measure acquisition rather than recovery of unlearned knowledge and are relinked to none. Two Table 1 misreads: (1) the Qwen3.5-9B disjoint values (R23–R26) are ES3, not ES5 (ES5 is about 93); (2) identical-prevention baselines (R27–R44) use GradDiff values instead of the single No Defense row. All results are single-seed. WMDP release accuracies after unlearning are not reported, so recovery size cannot be computed.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests whether fine-tuning can restore target behavior after output suppression, but does not establish near-chance release performance across the tested methods or compare all attacks against chance. It does not test prompting or quantization attacks.

The attacks use supervised full-parameter fine-tuning on 160 TOFU QA examples or larger WMDP corpora, not a few unrelated or loosely related examples. They do not isolate relearning from a subset of forgotten facts in all settings.

The study measures localized gate responses and gradient-path attenuation, but does not ablate a single activation direction to restore knowledge or directly prove that retained knowledge is blocked from access rather than deleted.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information as recovery attacks.

GSU is tested against downstream supervised fine-tuning and one tested benign-fine-tuning-then-attack sequence. It is not tested against quantization, prompt-only attacks, or every attack type in the claim.

labels.reason: Margin over best baseline under 1 point (34.13 vs RMU 34.83; 30.23 vs NPO 31.08), single seed; post-attack scores stay above chance.

relation.reason: The WMDP robust-removal results bear on A, B and F.

tranche.reason: The WMDP robust-removal setting (disjoint forget-corpus half, full-parameter attack, UWC-calibrated releases) is a new setting with results on A, B and F. It is not a specific argument that a version is wrong, so the reader's T5 does not fit. The study's method is not the relearning method it tests, so T2 adds nothing over T3.

source_check.notes: Table 2 is garbled in the text but placeable (rows in the order GradDiff, NPO, RMU, ...). No Defense = original Zephyr checkpoint after the same attack; release WMDP accuracy is never reported. WMDP attack: 150 full-parameter updates, lr 4e-6, batch 16, seed 0; F5 at step 125. TOFU results use a knowledge-absent base and do not bear on the claim.

statements.problem: Numbers right (NPO 36.39, RMU 34.83, No Defense 65.36, Bio F5 at step 125; release not reported). The 'thousands of documents' holds for the Bio pool (12,227) only; the Cyber pool behind R48/R49 is 500.

statements.correction: Bio attacker pool 12,227 docs (Cyber 500); 150 full-parameter updates, constant lr 4e-6, batch 16, 512-token sequences; F5 = step 125; all runs seed 0 (§E.5); releases UWC-calibrated to >=0.95 MMLU utility.
statements.problem: Numbers right. '12k Bio documents' is the attacker pool. The attack is 150 updates of 512-token sequences, not documents. The main WMDP comparison is also seed-0 single runs, not only the supplementary analyses.
RMU Bio 34.83 vs 65.36 (No Defense after the same attack) is right. Release accuracy is unreported, so 'partial recovery' is an upper bound, not a measured recovery.
Gives no GSU facts. R47/R50 are presumably cited through the 'also' list of authors' own tests, which is consistent with verdict l2 (F supports).

statements.correction: GSU F5 34.13 Bio, 30.23 Cyber; RMU 34.83 Bio, NPO 31.08 Cyber; No Defense (original checkpoint) after the same attack 65.36/43.83; release accuracy not reported; 125 of 150 full-parameter updates at lr 4e-6 on the disjoint forget-corpus half; seed 0.
statements.problem: GSU numbers right, but the lead claim that relearning 'brings back a large share' is not shown for GSU: release is unreported and 34.13 is far below 65.36. Also, 65.36/43.83 are No Defense after the same attack, not unattacked original values.
Matches the text: only supervised full-parameter fine-tuning attacks with one lr per setting (WMDP 4e-6) and seed 0. No LoRA or few-example attacks.
Numbers right: GSU 34.13 vs RMU 34.83 vs No Defense 65.36, all post-attack Bio F5.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: NPO and RMU on Qwen3.5-2B under the reported TOFU acquisition attack
reader_labels.reason: ES rises from release to after acquisition for both methods, contradicting the claim that the attack does not recover target behavior (R01–R02). The study does not quantify chance-level release performance for this condition.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NPO and RMU on Qwen3.5-2B under supervised fine-tuning on disjoint TOFU data
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports a clear release-to-post-acquisition rise in ES for both methods (R01–R02).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Reported TOFU and WMDP model comparisons, including GSU
reader_labels.reason: Post-attack scores vary by model, method, and prevention setting; GSU generally lowers acquisition relative to No Defense but does not eliminate measured scores. The attacks use more than a few examples (R03–R50).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected GSU gates at release on the reported B2 inputs
reader_labels.reason: The study finds lower selected-gate derivatives and increased negative-tail occupancy, consistent with local pathway attenuation (R53–R54).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Selected GSU gates after ten acquisition epochs
reader_labels.reason: Attacker fine-tuning partially reverses the measured gate attenuation, and the paper characterizes the evidence as local rather than proof of irreversible forgetting (R55–R56).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GSU against the tested downstream supervised fine-tuning attacks
reader_labels.reason: Across the reported TOFU and WMDP comparisons, GSU generally yields lower post-attack target scores than No Defense; the paper also reports an advantage after the tested benign adaptation (R06, R10, R14, R18, R22, R26, R29, R32, R35, R38, R41, R44, R47, R50, R57).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Scope of the tested GSU defense
reader_labels.reason: The evaluation covers specified supervised fine-tuning procedures and datasets; the paper notes limits on unrestricted retraining, proxy-to-attacker generalization, and broader settings. The internal response measures also show partial reversal (R55–R56).
